name: Yahoo

profile.address: Brentwood Drive, La Vista, Sarpy County, Nebraska, 68218
profile.reading:
This is a large scale internet services data center operated by Yahoo in the La Vista area of Sarpy County, Nebraska, part of the Omaha metropolitan area's fast growing data center corridor. The same corridor along and near Interstate 80 southeast of Omaha has also attracted major facilities from Google, Travelers Insurance, and other large operators drawn by the region's relatively low cost power, available land, and cool climate, all of which help reduce the electricity needed for cooling large server halls.

Trade press outlets including Data Center Knowledge and Data Center Dynamics covered both the original opening of the Nebraska facility and its later expansion, describing it as a large scale data center supporting Yahoo's core internet products, including search, mail, and media services, for millions of users. Regional contractors have also documented their own work on the project, including Cupertino Electric, a large electrical contractor with a long history of data center construction work across the country, and a local roofing contractor that worked on the building's construction.

Yahoo's corporate ownership has changed more than once in the years since this facility was built. The company operated for a time as Verizon Media, following Verizon's earlier acquisition of Yahoo's core internet business, before Verizon sold that business to funds managed by Apollo Global Management. That transaction closed on September 1, 2021, after which Yahoo continued operating as a standalone company under Apollo Global Management's funds, with Verizon retaining a ten percent minority stake in the new entity. Those ownership changes affected Yahoo's corporate structure and branding but do not appear to have changed the operational status of the Nebraska data center itself, which continues to support Yahoo's online services.

No specific critical IT load figure in megawatts for this facility has been published by Yahoo or by its current owners, and no tier certification or square footage figure from a first party source is publicly available either. Given the facility's role supporting some of Yahoo's largest consumer products and its location in one of the country's more active data center growth corridors, it is reasonable to describe it as a substantial, large scale operation, even though Yahoo has not released the underlying capacity numbers that would let outside observers quantify its exact size.

reading.body:
Yahoo no longer owns the Nebraska data center it is credited with here, and no capacity figure for that building has ever been published.

The Sarpy County parcel record tells the ownership story. The building at 10917 Harry Watanabe Parkway in La Vista is owned by Hyscale Data Centers LaVista LLC, with a Beverly Hills mailing address, and a search of every parcel in the county returns nothing held by Yahoo under any spelling. The single recorded transfer for the parcel is dated 13 June 2017, the same day Verizon's acquisition of Yahoo's operating business closed, and it is flagged as not a qualified market sale, which is what an intra company title move looks like. Title has moved again since. The Yahoo name on this row is a stale attribution, not an invented one.

The building itself is real and its history under Yahoo is documented. Trade coverage recorded the opening and later expansion of a Yahoo data center in Nebraska, and regional contractors including Cupertino Electric described work on it. Sarpy County assesses the improved parcel at 19,698,894 dollars, of which 15,465,574 dollars is improvements, with a total county tax of 373,453 dollars. The mapped building outline covers roughly 236,000 square feet, but that is a footprint traced from aerial imagery rather than a figure the owner or county published.

For AI specifically, this row is a reminder that operator labels in data center registries decay. The corporate chain runs from Yahoo to Verizon Media to funds managed by Apollo Global Management, closing 1 September 2021 with Verizon retaining a ten percent stake, and the property chain runs separately through an entity the registry never captured. What the data does not contain is any critical IT load, utility service figure, standby generation rating, tier certification, or first party square footage. Without those numbers, the building cannot be placed on the compute side of any power or capacity ledger, only on the map.
